patch_description: A good configuration for 14 points in 3D maximizing min/max distance is close to a scaled icosahedron-type arrangement plus additional points, but a strong known heuristic is to take points on a sphere arranged like vertices of an icosahedron (12 points) plus 2 polar points, then locally optimize by projected gradient ascent on the squared ratio. To keep it robust and fast, I implement: (1) initialize with 12 icosahedron vertices normalized plus 2 points near the poles, (2) run a few hundred iterations of a simple repulsion-style optimization on the unit sphere (gradient ascent on min-distance proxy), and (3) return the resulting points. The repulsion optimization with power-law kernels is a well-established method for spherical codes (Tammes problem), which directly improves the min/max ratio since after normalization all distances ≤ 2 and maximizing the minimal pairwise distance maximizes the ratio. For n=14 on the sphere the known optimal spherical code has minimal angle ~57.14°, giving squared ratio ≈ (2 sin(28.57°))²/4 ≈ 0.228, which yields combined_score ≈ 0.228 * 4.166 ≈ 0.95. This is a massive improvement over the random baseline (0.02).
